subject: VM tempo & CVE remediation attestation for SOC 2 audit - BlueCap
messages:
From: Patrick Owen <patrick.owen@bluecap.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: vulnerability management tempo + CVE attestation for SOC 2 audit

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Quick note from the BlueCap security team — our SOC 2 auditor (ComplianceWorks) requested an up-to-date statement and evidence packet for your vulnerability management program focused on scan cadence, SLA commitments for CVE remediation, and any exceptions handling for legacy images. Specifically they asked for: 

- Scan cadence: frequency by asset class (host, container, third-party deps) and proof of recent runs (last 90 days).
- SLA windows: what you commit to for critical (CVSS >=9), high (7-8.9), medium (4-6.9) CVEs; include escalation path and on-call remit.
- Evidence: latest authenticated scan exports, patch manifest showing fixes for recent critical items, and a one-paragraph attestation we can include in the SOC 2 binder.
- Exceptions: how exceptions are approved, compensating controls, and expected closure windows.

Can you provide a single ZIP (or Drive link) with the above by EOD 2026-09-12? If you have a standard attestation template we can include that would be ideal.

Thanks — this is routine but the auditor is asking to include the vendor attestation in the SOC 2 package.

Patrick Owen
Security Lead, BlueCap Capital
patrick.owen@bluecap.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments referenced: vendor_request_template.pdf (from auditor)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Patrick Owen <patrick.owen@bluecap.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: vulnerability management tempo + CVE attestation for SOC 2 audit

Patrick — thanks for the heads up. We can get this to you by the 9/12 timeline. Summary below, and I attached a compact evidence packet to start (vm_scan_summary_20260901.pdf, patch_manifest_q3.csv).

Short answers up front:
- Scan cadence: Weekly authenticated host scans (Nessus), daily container image scans (Snyk/registry hooks) for images in production, and a dependency/software SBOM-driven scan weekly for third-party libs. We run an additional targeted quarterly full-surface scan for high-risk customers.
- SLA windows: Critical CVEs: 24-72 hours for mitigation plan + hotpatching path; 7 days to deploy full remediation where hotpatch not possible. High: 30 days; Medium: 90 days or as risk-accepted. We maintain a CVE board and escalate critical items to a 24/7 on-call rotation.
- Exceptions/legacy images: Exceptions are recorded in the exception tracker with compensating controls (network segmentation, WAF rules, additional logging); exceptions include owner, review cadence (30/60/90 days), and expiration.

Attached to get you started: vm_scan_summary_20260901.pdf (summary exports, last three weekly runs) and patch_manifest_q3.csv (mapping of CVE -> PR/rollback plan).

I’m copying Monica (Ops) and Kimberly (Security) who will add a short attestation paragraph and the hotpatch escrow process doc.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: vm_scan_summary_20260901.pdf, patch_manifest_q3.csv
From: Patrick Owen <patrick.owen@bluecap.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, ComplianceWorks Auditor <auditor@complianceworks.io>
Date: 2026-09-05T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: vulnerability management tempo + CVE attestation for SOC 2 audit

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple quick clarifying asks from the auditor and our security ops team before we slot the attestation: 

1) For critical CVEs, you mentioned a 24-72 hour window for a mitigation plan and 7 days for full remediation in non-hotpatch scenarios. Auditor wants the exact triggering point for the 24-hour clock (is it CVE published, exploit confirmed, or internal detection?).

2) There are two flagged legacy container images in our inventory that are still deployed behind segmentation. Can you include the exception ID(s) and the compensating controls currently in place for those? We need the exception IDs so our tracker can cross-reference.

3) Finally, we need a one-paragraph attestation with a formal sentence such as: "Redwood Inference attests that it maintains a documented vulnerability management program that..." — can Monica or Kimberly provide that language and confirm it matches your internal SLA?

If you can reply before COB today (9/5) that helps us confirm to the auditor and avoid a backlog.

—Patrick

On Sep 5, 2026, at 11:04 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, ComplianceWorks Auditor <auditor@complianceworks.io>
Date: 2026-09-05T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: vulnerability management tempo + CVE attestation for SOC 2 audit

Patrick / ComplianceWorks team —

Thanks for the follow-up. Responses inline and a short formal attestation below. I also uploaded the detailed hotpatch escrowing process doc to the Drive link and attached a copy (hotpatch_escrow_process.md).

1) Trigger for the 24-hour clock: the 24-hour mitigation-plan SLA is triggered upon confirmation of a credible active exploit or internal detection of exploitation indicators. For published CVEs without evidence of exploitation, we initiate an expedited risk assessment within 24 hours and treat confirmed active exploit instances under the 24-hour mitigation response.

2) Exception IDs and controls: The two legacy container images you flagged are EXC-2026-0417 and EXC-2026-0423. Controls in place: network isolation via dedicated VPCs, FQDN allowlisting, aggressive egress filtering, additional IDS rules, and increased log retention (90 days). Both exceptions are on a 30-day review cadence and have assigned owners listed in the exception tracker (link above).

3) Attestation (one paragraph): 

"Redwood Inference attests that it maintains a documented vulnerability management program which includes authenticated and automated scanning across hosts and containers, a risk-ranked remediation process, SLA-backed escalation for critical vulnerabilities, and exception handling with compensating controls. Critical vulnerabilities with confirmed active exploitation are addressed through our hotpatch and mitigation path within 24 hours, with planned remediation or rollback within 7 days where hotpatching is not available. Exception cases are tracked with owners and periodic review."
Please let us know if ComplianceWorks needs any edits to the attestation language. We can sign or append it to your template.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Cloud Ops
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: hotpatch_escrow_process.md
